chapter_title: Concerning the Body: It was constructed after the Pattern of the Universe.
chapter_note: The dominant layer is CORE: systematic microcosm–macrocosm correspondences (body parts ↔ cosmic zones, five watch-stations, four bodily ‘worlds’ with sevens, and zodiac-to-body schemas). A later PASTORAL graft (¶17–24) reuses the cosmological pattern to interpret ethical self-mastery and the ‘elect’ life; this crosses from cosmos→cosmos mapping into cosmos→community/behavior application. The chapter is wrapped and re-started by small FRAME dialogue-attribution formulas (¶1, ¶30, ¶37). No NT/explicit Gospel overlay appears.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic scene-setting: ‘the apostle … among the church … congregation … says to his disciples’. This is compilation-frame language, not impersonal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: This whole universe, above and below, reflects the pattern of the human body; as the formation of this body of flesh accords to the pattern of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Programmatic correspondential thesis stated impersonally: universe↔body patterning (microcosm/macrocosm) without institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: Its head is like the first-fruits of the five garments. And, from its neck down to the site of its heart, it resembles the pattern of the ten firmaments. And again, the heart accords to the wheel of the rotating sphere. And, from its heart down to its intestines (?), is like this atmosphere that extends from the sphere down to the earth. The [male] part of the body corresponds to this great earth. And also, from its intestines (?) down to its loins is like the three earths. And also, its shinbones to the pattern of the space in which the Porter stands. Its footsoles to the great earth upon which the Porter is stood; and the four fastenings that are under his feet. Its liver to the vessel of fire. Its flesh to the vessel of darkness. Its blood to the vessel of water.
paragraphs.temporal_note: High-density systematic mapping (body regions/organs ↔ cosmic structures: garments/firmaments/sphere/earths/Porter/vessels). Both sides remain inside the cosmological architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, this is how the small body corresponds to the macro-cosmos in its firmaments, in its orderings, in its mountains, its walls and its vessels, as I have made clear to you!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative closure of a correspondential schema; minor 2nd-person address does not pivot to institutional discipline and stays within the same cosmic mapping register.

paragraphs.core_text: Once more, I reveal to you: There exist five great camps in this great outer zone, of which the five sons of the Living Spirit are masters.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered/structured cosmology (‘five camps’, ‘five sons of the Living Spirit’) in impersonal expository mode—typical core architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: So, in the first watch-station above, of which the Keeper of Splendour is master, on the battlement of all the works, is found his authority over the three heavens. Then the ones below him [ ... ... ] the great King of Honour.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic administration by named beings and ranked ‘watch-station’ structure; lacunae do not change the clearly systematic cosmological layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The second watch, of which the great King of Honour is master, his own authority (extends) over the seven firmaments beneath him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree/number structure (second watch; seven firmaments) within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The third watch, of which the Adamant [is master, his authority] reigns from the firmament down below to the [earth]. [And he] invigorates, according to his authority, the sphere and the worlds of the atmosphere; and the other four worlds that are appointed on this earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos exposition with hierarchical ‘authority’ language and world-stratification; no community/application pivot.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.171⟩
The fourth watch, over which the King of Glory has power, is the three wheels. And his authority lies over the three earths upon the head of the Porter.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core numbered schema: watch-station ↔ wheels/earths/Porter (internal cosmography).

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth watch is the watch over which the Porter is authoritative. Again, he is master, according to his authority, over this great earth he stands upon, and the four fastenings under his feet.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the five-watch structure; purely cosmological correspondences.

paragraphs.core_text: Affliction has come about in these five watches from time to time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Transitional cosmic-historical note introducing conflicts within the watch-stations; still internal to the cosmological narrative.

paragraphs.core_text: So, in the watch of the Keeper of Splendour, Sin desired to spurt up towards the image of the Ambassador. Yet, they barred it from that place, and it fell back down in shame.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic conflict within the cosmic system; ‘Sin’ acts as an agent (personified cosmological force), not moral exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, an earthquake and treachery occurred in the watch of the great King of Honour, which the watchers who had arisen at the time and had [ ... ] they who were sent came down, until they were humbled.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic disturbance narrative tied to the watch-station hierarchy; no institutional target.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, in the watch of the Adamant, the abortions came to the earth and fashioned [the] figure of flesh.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmogonic event-language (generation of ‘figure of flesh’) located within the watch-station system—still core mythic mechanics.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, in the watch of the King of Glory, a commotion happened in these three earths above the Porter. The pathway was obstructed for the ascent of these three wheels; that of wind, that of water, and that of fire.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core: structured cosmos with three wheels (wind/water/fire) and obstructed ascent—mechanistic cosmology.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, in the watch of the Porter, the fastenings beneath were laid bare and strained their chains. A great earthquake befell that place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completion of the five-watch affliction sequence; still internal to cosmic geography (Porter/fastenings/chains).

Editorial application pivot: ‘this is also the case with this body that the elect wear’ shifts the correspondence from cosmic structure to community identity (‘elect’), using the cosmology to interpret lived religious status.
Moralizing application (‘elect person … guide it towards the good’) aligning self-control with a cosmic ruler; correspondence now points to behavioral discipline.
‘Whoever will become master…’ ethical interiorization of the cosmic hierarchy; still an application register rather than impersonal cosmography.
Explicit ascetic control of lust/genitals; cosmos used as exemplar (‘mystery of the Adamant… subdues Matter’) in service of discipline—application layer.
Purifying nourishment and mastering inner fire is practical-ethical instruction; cosmic comparison is in service of conduct.
Behavioral exhortation (‘bind it with the chain of peace’) framed through a cosmic analogy; the mapping points outward to practice.
Defines ‘teaching of wisdom … in that body’ by likeness to Virgin of Light—still a spiritualizing application to persons rather than a cosmographic map.
Virtue-list (‘love and joy, faith and truth’) and ‘the person should live’ are classic pastoral/ethical diction; light-ship imagery is applied to personal salvation.

paragraphs.core_text: Once more, understand this other (truth): There exist four worlds in this body of the flesh, and there exist countless times seven rulers in the body of the four worlds!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Returns to enumerated anatomical-cosmological schema (four worlds; sevens) in descriptive mode; no ‘elect’/disciplinary targeting.

paragraphs.core_text: So, the first world is from its neck up; and also the seven rulers who are in this upper world are these: the two organs of sight, and the two of hearing, and the two of smell. The other one is the mouth, which is the organ of taste.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic listing by number, mapping ‘world’ to sensory organs; correspondence remains structural.

paragraphs.core_text: The second world is from its neck down to its entire upper torso. And also, the seven rulers who are in this second world are: its two arms that accord to the pattern of its two ears, which occur in its first world above; and its two breasts that are to the pattern of its organs of smell; and the two eyes of its heart; and the gullet of the stomach between the two breasts, which in the chest is the pattern of the mouth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Microcosmic correspondential reasoning (‘accord to the pattern’) with internal analogies; no institutional address.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.173⟩
Once more, there exist seven rulers in the third world of the body, which are these: the fat, the lung, the spleen, the liver, the gall, and its two kidneys.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure enumerative schema (seven rulers) tied to organs—typical core catalog style.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the fourth world below. There are another seven there of this same kind: its two buttocks (?), and its two testicles, and its two loins; and the member out of which the seed comes, that begets all the forms.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Anatomical ‘fourth world’ completes the fourfold structure; ‘begets all the forms’ reads as cosmological-anthropogonic mechanism rather than moral exhortation.
Dialogue-attribution formula (‘the enlightener speaks to his hearers’)—compilation frame marker; not part of the substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Aries and Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces; these are the twelve signs of the zodiac that occur in the worlds above, on the sphere. They are interlocked and bound on this turning wheel, the one in which they are [ ... ], fixed, and planted. And, regarding all these twelve signs of the zodiac, this is how they were appointed and made leaders [ ... ] on the sphere beneath the heaven that is the wheel of the stars. Now, they are appointed like this, they are thus, so that you can find the head of [ ... ] and you find the tail too [ ... ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Astrological-cosmological catalog of the twelve, located ‘above, on the sphere’ with wheel mechanics; the explanatory aside does not introduce church/ethics.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, they occur like this, these that we have recited, one after another in this body. They are counted by order and number from the head to the feet. Its head is Aries. Its neck and its shoulders are Taurus. Its two arms Gemini. Its upper torso is Cancer. Its stomach is Leo. Its belly is Virgo. The vertical spine and its intestines (?) are Libra. Its genitals Scorpio. Its loins are Sagittarius. Its knees are Capricorn. Its shinbones are Aquarius. The soles of its feet are Pisces.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic correspondential body-map (zodiac→body) presented as a numbered ordered schema; fully internal mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: Behold, these are also distributed one after another. They exist in this body, as if turned to the side and bent to the pattern of the twelve signs of the zodiac. They too are thus, arranged one against another, head to tail, as they occur on the wheel [ ... ] up.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Technical description of a second arrangement (‘turned to the side’, ‘head to tail’) matching the zodiac wheel—system description, not exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, they are counted by order and number of the body and all its members. So, we have proclaimed that these are turned to the side, bent, and spread out; because from its head down to its hip shall count six to its left, and another six to its right.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the formal counting schema (six left/six right), maintaining impersonal instructional cosmography.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.174⟩
The six that are down its right are these that I will recount: the right temple is Aries; its right shoulder is Taurus; its right arm is Gemini; its right rib-cage is Cancer; its stomach is Leo; the right side of its reproductive organs are Virgo.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Further elaboration of the second zodiac-body schema; list form is characteristic of the core substrate’s correspondential catalogs.

paragraphs.core_text: Conversely, the other six about which we have spoken, which are to its left, in contrast they come from its hip to its head: its left [ ... ] is Libra; its left rib-cage is Scorpio; its left breast and left kidney is Sagittarius; its [left] elbow is Capricorn; its left shoulder is Aquarius; its left temple is Pisces. This is how the creator of the body himself has appointed them. He has [set] them in order and arranged them, one against its companion, head to tail.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the left-side sequence and closes with creator-ordering rationale; still an internal system description (appointment/order).
Short speech-transition formula (‘Once more he speaks’)—editorial framing device.

paragraphs.core_text: Listen to this other lesson that I will proclaim to you. Understand that there exist many powers in this body. They are the house-dwellers who are made the leaders in it. There are eight hundred and forty times ten thousand rulers made chiefs in the human body! They are distributed and set firm, quartered according to house. The count and number of their houses is two hundred and ten times ten thousand.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite introductory address, the content is a numeric/structural catalog of inner ‘powers’ and ‘houses’ (microcosmic polity), consistent with core enumerative teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: When all these rulers come creeping and moving within the body, they will meet one another; and they shall beset and destroy one another, and [ ... ] in them there. When [ ... t/il]] they shall erupt from the body of the person who [will] die; and make putrid boils and sores and burning wounds in the body. Either they might have made him sick within; or else they might come forth upon his outer side. Those wounds shall first be squeezed and discharge their liquid, and empty out their pus, until they are squeezed [ ... ... ] and the suppuration forced out from the wound. Afterwards, their scars shall close over; and they are healed and obtain relief from the places that came out upon them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mechanistic microcosm physiology/demonology (rulers moving, erupting as sores) described as process; no institutional exhortation or NT citation.
